Committee: Health
Sponsor: Hollis
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 04/26/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 639 as introduced would increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Public Health by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of eyelash extension facilities the Department must license, regulate, and inspect as provided for by this bill. The increase in obligation will be offset, in total or in part, by licensure fees collected by the Department of $250 for an initial license, $200 for renewal of an annual license, and $50 for a temporary license to operate at a fixed location for not more than two weeks.
In addition, this bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
Paul W. Lee, Chair
Health

Committee: Economic Development and Tourism
Sponsor: Gudger
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 04/23/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 384 as passed the Senate allows counties, beginning October 1, 2021, to levy sales tax on the sale of alcoholic beverages in certain community development districts at the same rate as the sale of beer and wine in the largest municipality in the county in which the district is established. This bill provides that the tax proceeds shall be deposited into a special fund in the county treasury to be used for grants to support education, civic, community, and tourism activities within the county, and that the grants shall be distributed based on the recommendations of each legislator representing a portion of the county in which the funds are collected, based on the proportion of the population the legislator represents in the county.
Becky Nordgren, Chair
Economic Development and Tourism
